faq: What is the difference between a slat and a panel?

A slat is a narrow strip (usually 10–40 cm wide and 2.90 m long) installed side by side, often fluted. A panel is wide (about 96–122 cm) and covers a large area at once, for example in marble, travertine or concrete look.
PVC or SPC — what is the difference?
Both are low-maintenance synthetic materials. SPC (stone-polymer composite) is denser and more rigid; PVC is lighter and easy to cut. The material is shown on the product page when known.
Yes, all prices include Israeli VAT. For products without a price, the price is given with your quote.

guideDesc: Slats or panels, PVC or SPC, measuring your wall and calculating quantities — a short, clear guide.
guide: Fluted slats create a vertical rhythm, make the room feel taller and are perfect for TV walls, headboards and entrances. Wide panels suit large surfaces and give a continuous marble, travertine or concrete look with few joints.

A narrow slat (15–17 cm) gives a fine, dense look; 20 cm is the balanced standard; a smooth 40 cm slat is often used as a calm surface between fluted areas. Groove width changes the play of shadow: wide, rounded grooves stand out more in side light.
Gloss reflects light and brings out marble veins — ideal for bathrooms, living rooms and entrances. Matte hides fingerprints and suits stone, plaster and concrete textures.

Measure width and height in several places and keep the largest value. Mark sockets, switches and openings. If the wall is taller than one unit (usually 2.80–2.90 m), plan a joint or a finishing profile.
On a flat, dry wall, use a strong hybrid adhesive. For a clean finish, combine skirting, cornices and moldings — all available in the catalog.
